01 / THE PROBLEM — BEFORE

Another evening.
Another AI success story.

Someone nearby, with less skill than you, has made over $5k selling simple AI solutions.

You ask, “When is it my turn?”

Maybe you watched the dot-com boom. Then regular people turned social media into a living. Each time, it felt like you were watching from the sidelines.

Now your feed is full of “I made $15,000 with AI” videos. You save another one. But the excitement fades when you still don’t know what to make, who would buy it, or how to begin.

You want a way in—something you can build without walking away from your day job.

So why haven’t you started?

Because every attempt seems to hit the same three walls.

“I’m not technical.”

APIs. Python. Complex automations. You came to learn a useful skill, not start a computer science degree.

“The output is generic.”

You type a prompt, get a robotic answer, and close the tab. Where’s the part a business would actually pay for?

“There’s too much noise.”

Another 10,000-prompt pack. Still no clear answer to what to sell, who needs it, or what to say.
